infoText.about: Showing up is the goal. After 50, consistency is more important than sets or reps. Keep moving, stay injury-free, feel good doing it.
infoText.setsAndReps: I usually do 3 sets with a 1/2 weight add-on finisher. Somewhere between 10 and 15 reps where the last few feel like work but form never breaks. Rest usually 2 minutes per set.
infoText.floor: Three movements per session. Primary option first, alternative after the slash — use whichever is free. No supersets, no circuits. Do your sets, rest, move on.
infoText.burnout: Optional. Drop your main compound to 50–60% of working weight and take it to failure. Aim for 20–30 reps. Maintains muscle without heavy loading.
infoText.mat: Over time you should develop your own stretch and core routine using the suggestions here. What we suggest here augments what you already know. The hamstring stretch is a daily constant. Everything else rotates. Props are always optional.
infoText.whenToGo: No streaks. No guilt. The app picks up exactly where you left off — tomorrow or next week, it does not matter.

rules.moveOn: Hit the target with clean form 2 sessions in a row.
rules.regress: Pain, a giving-out feeling, form breaking down, or can't reach the bottom of the range. Also regress if you have to arch your back to reach the position.

phases.name: Phase 1: Shoulder Foundation
phases.goal: Left cuff strength, right shoulder range, safe pressing, core and hamstrings. Worth doing for its own sake.
warmup: Wrist rocks on all fours: 10 fingers forward, 10 back
Wrist push-ups (rock up onto fingers): 2 x 10
Right shoulder: lying dowel overhead reach, ribs down: 10

ladders.name: Mat · Plank progression
ladders.cue: Hold first, then the single-arm work in the same set. On the wall: back your feet up and place your toes at the mark, press toes into the wall, hands stay planted. Shift weight slowly, grip the floor, stop before the shoulder gives. Wall marks at 1, 2 and 3 ft (tape or wall features). Roller step: press it with a foot first to check it's wedged before putting weight on it. Have a medicine ball? Rolling it under one hand works for the fingertip-hover step too.

steps.name: Floor plank: 30s hold, then 10 weight shifts
Floor plank: 30s hold, then 6 fingertip hovers each side (palm up onto fingertips, then lift 1 inch)
Floor plank: 20s hold, then 6 shoulder taps each side
Feet on the low bar (~4"): 20s hold, then 6 shoulder taps each side
Feet on foam roller on the low bar, wedged against the wall (~10"): 20s hold, then 6 shoulder taps each side
steps.dose: 3 sets · NEEDS FOAM ROLLER + LOW BAR + WALL

Feet on wall at 2 ft: 20s hold, then 4 shoulder taps each side
Feet on wall at 3 ft: 20s hold, then 3 shoulder taps each side

ladders.name: Mat · Pike hold
ladders.cue: Ears between biceps, chest toward thighs. Tight hamstrings: bend your knees a little so your back stays flat and arms stay in line with your ears. Legs straighten as flexibility improves. Ribs down: if your back arches to get your arms overhead, bring your hands forward. Your right shoulder has less range; don't force it.

ladders.name: Mat · Pike shrugs
ladders.cue: Elbows locked, full range, pause at the top. Tight hamstrings: bend your knees a little so your back stays flat and arms stay in line with your ears. Legs straighten as flexibility improves. Ribs down: if your back arches to get your arms overhead, bring your hands forward. Your right shoulder has less range; don't force it.

ladders.name: Mat · Pike push-ups
ladders.cue: Head lands slightly in front of hands, elbows back at 45°. Tight hamstrings: bend your knees a little so your back stays flat and arms stay in line with your ears. Legs straighten as flexibility improves. Ribs down: if your back arches to get your arms overhead, bring your hands forward. Your right shoulder has less range; don't force it.

steps.name: Knee-drop pike push-ups: lower in pike, knees drop at the bottom, press up from knees, lift back into pike

ladders.name: Machines · Dip support hold
ladders.cue: Shoulders pushed down, away from ears. No jumping: use the station's built-in steps to get into position.

steps.name: Support hold, feet lightly on floor

ladders.name: Machines · Assisted dips
ladders.cue: Kneel or stand on the pad. Shoulders pushed down away from your ears, only go as deep as feels stable. Less weight on the stack = harder.

steps.name: Assisted dip machine, moderate assist, 3s lowering

ladders.name: Machines · Half-kneeling dumbbell press
ladders.cue: Half-kneeling, one arm at a time. Press only as high as your ribs stay down; stop before your back arches. The right arm may stop short of vertical, that's fine.

ladders.name: Machines · Single-arm overhead hold
ladders.cue: One arm at a time. Hold only as high as your ribs stay down; the right arm may sit in front of your ear. Add 5 lb only with zero wobble and no arch.

ladders.name: Mat · Dead bugs
ladders.cue: Lower back flat.

ladders.name: Mat · Hollow hold
ladders.cue: Exhale, ribs down. Shorten the hold before letting the back arch.

ladders.name: Mat · Band external rotations
ladders.cue: Light band, slow, elbow tucked at your side. Pain-free.

ladders.name: Machines · Inverted rows
ladders.cue: Body straight, pull chest to the bar, squeeze shoulder blades together.

ladders.name: Machines · Pulldown → assisted pull-ups
ladders.cue: No jumping. Step up onto the machine's platform to reach the bar. Shoulders pulled down first, then pull with the arms. Lower slowly.

ladders.name: Machines · Y-T-W raises
ladders.cue: Slow, thumbs up, squeeze the shoulder blades. Shoulder stability without hanging. Ribs down: if your back arches to get your arms overhead, bring your hands forward. Your right shoulder has less range; don't force it.

ladders.cue: Elbow under shoulder, hips high, body in one line.

ladders.name: Machines · Supported hang
ladders.cue: Bar about head height, feet stay on the floor, lean back into a long banana stretch. Take as much weight on your feet as you need. Shoulders stay active, not dangling. Ribs down: if your back arches to get your arms overhead, bring your hands forward. Your right shoulder has less range; don't force it. Left shoulder: stay active, never sink into the stretch.

ladders.name: Mat · Forearm headstand prep
ladders.cue: Elbows shoulder-width, press forearms into the floor and push the chest toward your legs. Tight hamstrings: bend your knees a little so your back stays flat and arms stay in line with your ears. Legs straighten as flexibility improves. Ribs down: if your back arches to get your arms overhead, bring your hands forward. Your right shoulder has less range; don't force it.

steps.name: Dolphin hold, feet walked in a little
Dolphin hold, feet walked in, shoulders over elbows

ladders.name: Mat · Ball rollout
ladders.cue: Ribs down, glutes squeezed, back flat. Only roll as far as you can without your lower back sagging. Ab wheel instead? It's much harder: only after full ball rollouts, kneeling, rolling toward a wall to limit range.

steps.name: Kneeling, forearms on ball, short roll out
Kneeling, roll out until arms are overhead

ladders.name: Mat · Slow leg lowers
ladders.cue: Lower back pressed into the floor. Only lower as far as you can without it lifting. This trains the controlled lowering for donkey kicks.

ladders.name: Mat · Hamstrings & pike stretch
ladders.cue: Gentle, never bounce. Lead with the chest and keep the back long. Progress comes over months, not sessions.

steps.name: Lying hamstring stretch with band, other leg flat
Band stretch + contract-relax: press leg into band 5s, relax, ease deeper
Standing pike fold, knees soft, flat back, hands to shins
Seated pike fold, flat back, contract-relax

ladders.name: Mat · Right shoulder mobility
ladders.cue: Right (repaired) shoulder. Slow, gentle, never force or bounce. Ribs down and lower back flat: the moment your back arches, you've reached your real range. Left shoulder: do the upper-back and lat parts, but skip the end-range shoulder stretches on that side.

steps.name: Foam roller upper-back extension + child's pose lat stretch
Add: lying dowel overhead reach, ribs down
Add: right cross-body stretch and sleeper stretch
steps.dose: 2 x 30s each · NEEDS FOAM ROLLER + DOWEL

steps.dose: 2 x 30s · NEEDS FOAM ROLLER + DOWEL + BENCH

steps.name: Full routine, then wall slides ribs down, right arm a little higher each week
steps.dose: 2 x 10 · NEEDS FOAM ROLLER + DOWEL + BENCH + WALL

ladders.name: Mat · Left shoulder stability
ladders.cue: Left shoulder (past dislocations): strength, not stretch. Light weight, slow, perfect control. Avoid the arm out to the side and rotated back position, and never hang or stretch into end range on this side.

steps.name: Add: lying serratus punch (press up, reach the ceiling), 5-8 lb
Add: bottoms-up kettlebell hold, light, elbow bent 90°

phases.graduation: Reach the last step of every ladder and hit its target.
extraChecks: Wrist rocks: 20 reps, pain-free the next day
One full week with no shoulder pain or slipping feeling
Wall test logged: how high your right thumb reaches overhead with back and ribs flat against the wall

phases.name: Phase 3: Forearm Headstand

phases.goal: Only if the right-shoulder wall test passes and the left shoulder has been solid for months: wall walks, chest-to-wall holds, wall shoulder taps. No kick-ups or freestanding work.
